content: 1. Facilities 567 included residents aged 12 to 21 years who had a positive nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT) result. Exclusion criteria included pregnancy, breastfeeding, gonorrhea co-infection, allergy to tetracyclines or macrolides, previous photosensitivity from doxycycline, inability to swallow pills, receipt of an antibiotic with antichlamydial activity within 21 days before screening or between screening and enrollment, concomitant infection requiring treatment with an antibiotic with antichlamydial activity, and pelvic inflammatory disease or epididymitis. Outcomes measured were microbiological cure and adverse events. Treatments included azithromycin 1 g as a single dose or doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days. 2. In a study conducted in Turkey in 2005, sexually active, non-pregnant women of reproductive age or early menopause (aged 18–52 years) who attended clinics due to various symptoms were included. Exclusion criteria were treatment with another antimicrobial agent within the previous two weeks and known hypersensitivity to macrolides or tetracyclines. Outcomes measured were microbiological cure, with treatments including azithromycin 1 g as a single dose or doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days. 3. A 1993 study in the USA included adolescent men and women aged 15–20 years with chlamydial infection, provided they were not pregnant or nursing and had not taken antibiotics within 72 hours before study entry. Exclusion criteria included significant hepatic, renal, cardiac, or hematologic diseases, known allergy to study drugs, evidence of gonococcal pharyngitis, proctitis, or disseminated gonococcal infection. Outcomes measured were microbiological cure and adverse events, with treatments including azithromycin 1 g as a single dose or doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days. 4. A 1993 study in Finland included symptomatic adult men aged 18–60 years with signs and symptoms compatible with nongonococcal urethritis (e.g., dysuria, urethral irritation, or discharge, or at least four white blood cells per high-power field on microscopy of a methylene blue-stained urethral smear). Exclusion criteria included treatment with another antimicrobial agent within the previous two weeks, known hypersensitivity to macrolides and tetracyclines, evidence of any gastrointestinal condition that might affect study drug administration, and presence of intracellular diplococci in the methylene blue stain of the urethral smear. Outcomes measured were microbiological cure and adverse events, with treatments including azithromycin 1 g as a single dose or doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days. 5. A 1993 study in the United Kingdom included adult men aged 19–57 years with symptoms and/or signs of nongonococcal urethritis (NGU), such as discharge, dysuria, or urethral irritation, and with ≥5 polymorphonuclear leukocytes. Exclusion criteria included gram-negative intracellular diplococci in the urethral smear, treatment with another antimicrobial agent within two weeks of enrollment, other associated infections requiring treatment with another antimicrobial agent in addition to the study drug, or allergy to macrolides or tetracyclines. Outcomes measured were microbiological cure, clinical cure, and adverse events, with treatments including azithromycin 1 g as a single dose or doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days. 6. A 2013 study in the USA included males aged ≥16 years who were English speakers with visible urethral discharge on examination or ≥5 polymorphonuclear leukocytes per high-power field on a Gram-stained slide of urethral exudates. Exclusion criteria included receipt of antibiotics in the past month or allergies to study drugs. Outcomes measured were microbiological cure and adverse events, with treatments including azithromycin 1 g as a single dose or doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days. 7. A 1992 study in the USA included men and women with presumptive chlamydial urethral and/or endocervical infection. Exclusion criteria included evidence of gonococcal pharyngitis, proctitis, or disseminated gonococcal infection; treatment with a systemic antibiotic within 72 hours before enrollment; evidence of salpingitis or epididymitis; history of allergy or hypersensitivity to erythromycin or doxycycline; history of a serious underlying chronic disease; a positive test for hepatitis B surface antigen; known alcohol or drug abuse; and pregnancy or lactation. Outcomes measured were microbiological cure and adverse events, with treatments including azithromycin 1 g as a single dose or doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days. 8. A 2011 study in the USA included heterosexual men aged 18–65 years. Exclusion criteria included a positive test result for gonorrhea at the baseline visit, history of recurrent NGU (>3 episodes within the previous year) or recent NGU (within the previous 30 days), signs or symptoms of epididymitis or prostatitis, known allergy to study drugs, receipt of systemic antibiotics within 30 days of enrollment, presence of concomitant infection requiring antibiotics, unwillingness to abstain from alcohol for 24 hours after enrollment, serious underlying infection (including known HIV infection or other primary or secondary immunosuppression), or voiding within the hour preceding evaluation. Outcomes measured were microbiological cure and adverse events, with treatments including azithromycin 1 g as a single dose or doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days. 9. A 2000 study in Turkey included women with signs and symptoms compatible with mucopurulent cervicitis (e.g., purulent endocervical discharge, edema, erythema, and friability of the zone of ectopy). Exclusion criteria included treatment with another antimicrobial agent within the previous two weeks, known hypersensitivity to macrolides and tetracyclines, evidence of any gastrointestinal condition that might affect study drug administration, and presence of diplococci in the Gram stain of the cervical smear. Outcomes measured were microbiological cure, with treatments including azithromycin 1 g as a single dose or doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days. 10. A 1995 study in the USA included adult men aged ≥18 years with typical symptoms of urethritis. Exclusion criteria included Gram’s stain or subsequent culture evidence of gonococcal infection, other significant systemic disease, a urological abnormality, known HIV infection, allergy to erythromycin or doxycycline, necessity for treatment with another antibiotic, treatment with an investigational drug in the last 30 days, antimicrobial therapy in the last two weeks, or a gastrointestinal condition that would likely affect drug absorption. Outcomes measured were microbiological cure, clinical cure, and adverse events, with treatments including azithromycin 1 g as a single dose or doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days. 11. A 1994 study in Iceland included males aged 16–48 years with symptoms of urethritis diagnosed by urethral culture. Exclusion criteria were not reported. Outcomes measured were microbiological cure and adverse events, with treatments including azithromycin 1 g as a single dose or doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days.
